intro: Chrome for social media managers on Mac works best with one profile per brand or client. Each profile keeps its own bookmarks, history, passwords, and settings, so one client's tools never mix with another's. This page covers profile setup, tab groups, shortcuts, a daily routine, and where Lazur helps while you work in Chrome.

Profiles are not a security boundary. Anyone with access to your Mac can switch to any profile on it.
Hootsuite's guideline estimates put daily checks between about 55 minutes and 1 hour 45 minutes.
Chrome 152 is the latest verified stable Mac release, out September 1, 2026. Check Chrome > About Google Chrome for yours.

blocks.text: Why one profile per client beats one crowded window

Most social media managers start with one Chrome window. Within a week it holds the scheduler, three inboxes, an analytics tab, a Canva file, and a few mention searches. Finding the right tab takes longer than doing the task.

Profiles split the browser into separate rooms. Each profile keeps its own bookmarks, history, passwords, and other settings. Your client's ad account can live in one profile, and your personal email in another.

This matters most when you run several brands from one Mac. A wrong click in the wrong profile can reply, post, or change a setting for the wrong account. Separate profiles make that mistake less likely. They do not make it impossible, so keep checking the profile icon before you act.
Set up Chrome profiles for each brand on Mac

Start with the profile icon in the top right corner of the Chrome window. Click it, then add a new profile. Name each profile after the brand, not after yourself. A name like Brand A Ads or Client B Scheduler saves you a second look later.

items: Open Chrome and click the profile icon at the top right.
Add a new profile and follow the prompts to name it after the brand.
Sign in only with the account that belongs to that brand, if the brand uses a Google sign in.
Save passwords for the brand's tools inside that profile only.
Pin the scheduler and the main inbox, then bookmark the tools you use every day.
Run one real task in the new profile before you close the window.

blocks.text: To switch later, click the profile icon and choose the profile. Chrome then loads that profile's bookmarks and history. Your other profiles stay separate, so a saved password in one never fills a field in another.

blocks.title: Profiles are not locks
blocks.text: Anyone with access to your Mac can switch to any profile on it. Removing a profile permanently erases its bookmarks, history, passwords, and settings from the computer. Export anything you need before you delete a profile.
Tab groups and keyboard shortcuts in Chrome on Mac

Profiles hold the logins. Tab groups hold the tabs for one task. Put the comment inbox, the DM inbox, and your reply template document into one group called Replies. Collapse the group when you move on to planning.

The Google help page I read covers tab groups on Android, not on a Mac. It says a group syncs across devices signed in to the same Google Account. It also says tab groups cannot be pinned, and a group unused for 14 days moves to Inactive. Check the desktop help before you rely on those rules. On a Mac, try right-clicking a tab to find the group option, since menu wording changes.
Keyboard shortcuts cut the back and forth between tabs. These are standard Chrome shortcuts on macOS.

items: ⌘T opens a new tab. ⌘W closes the current tab.
⌘⇧T reopens the last tab you closed. Press it again to go further back.
⌘1 through ⌘8 jump to tabs one to eight. ⌘9 jumps to the last tab.
⌘L moves the cursor to the address bar.
⌘Y opens History. ⌘D bookmarks the page you are on.
⌘⇧N opens a new incognito window, useful for seeing a post the way a logged out visitor sees it.
⌘, opens Chrome Settings.

blocks.text: Pick five shortcuts you will use every day. Drill those for a week. Learning every shortcut at once rarely sticks.
Daily social media tasks in Chrome: what to check and when

Hootsuite's guideline estimates list three daily jobs. Replies to comments and DMs take 30 to 60 minutes. Monitoring brand mentions takes 15 to 30 minutes. Reviewing scheduled posts takes 10 to 15 minutes. Hootsuite calls one to two hours a day a good starting point for these checks.
Those figures are guidelines, not survey data. They still make a useful frame. The table shows one way to split a day for one client in Chrome.

blocks.caption: Sample layout for one client. The times are examples, not Hootsuite figures.

blocks.text: Batch replies in one sitting. Switching in and out of a comment thread every few minutes costs more attention than the replies themselves. Give the Replies group one block of time, then close it.
Mention checks and scheduled posts without losing your place
Pin the scheduler and the main inbox in each profile. A pinned tab stays small at the left edge of the tab bar, so it stays in view. If it is your first tab, jump to it with ⌘1.
Leave mention searches in a group instead. Collapse that group when you do not need it. Pinned tabs and grouped tabs solve different problems, so use both.
Edge case: a scheduler that keeps asking you to sign in is often a profile problem. Check the profile icon at the top right before you reset any passwords. You may be inside another client's profile.
Weekly planning, batching, and reporting for social media managers

Hootsuite's weekly estimates set the rhythm of the week. Planning and scheduling posts takes 1 to 2 hours. Creating and batching content takes 1 to 3 hours. Routing posts for approval takes 15 to 30 minutes. A weekly performance report takes 30 to 60 minutes.

Take a three brand week as a worked example. Each brand has its own profile, so you move between them without signing in again. If each report takes the top of Hootsuite's range, the three reports alone take three hours. Plan for that, or cut the report down to one dashboard per brand.

items: Monday: plan and schedule posts, one profile at a time.
Tuesday and Wednesday: batch captions and graphics in one document, then move them into each scheduler.
Thursday: send posts for approval and note the changes in the Replies group.
Friday: pull the weekly reports from each profile's analytics tab.

blocks.text: Keep batching separate from the scheduler. Writing captions inside the scheduler tab invites small edits that eat the afternoon. Draft in a plain document, then paste the final version once.
Common Chrome mistakes that cost social media managers time

items: Running one profile for every client. One wrong click can post to the wrong brand.
Signing into a client account in your personal profile, then forgetting to sign out.
Assuming tab groups stay open forever. The Android help page says unused groups move to Inactive after 14 days, so check how your Mac behaves.
Deleting a profile to clean up. That erases its bookmarks, history, passwords, and settings from the Mac.
Letting Chrome fall behind. An old version can break a page you need during a launch.
Keeping every tab you have ever opened. A crowded tab bar hides the one you need.

blocks.text: Most of these come from speed. The fix is a short review at the end of each day. Close what you finished, and move what you still need into its group.
Chrome version and macOS support in 2026
The latest verified Mac stable release is Chrome 152. Google released it on September 1, 2026. Chrome 151 came out on August 7, 2026. To see your version, choose Chrome > About Google Chrome.

Chrome 150 is the last release that supports macOS 12. Chrome 151 and later no longer support it. Existing macOS 12 installs keep running, but they stop getting updates. If your Mac still runs macOS 12, a macOS upgrade is the real fix.

Release timing is less settled. Google's download page says there is a new update every four weeks. Google's enterprise notes say Chrome moves to a two-week cycle from Chrome 153. The Chrome Releases blog lists an early stable update dated November 4, 2026, without a version number.

blocks.title: Check before you plan around a date
blocks.text: Open Chrome > About Google Chrome and compare your version with the Chrome Releases blog. Do this before a launch, not during one.
What the workload surveys say about social media work

Metricool ran a 2026 well-being study of people who create and manage social content. It is a vendor study. Its page says over 1,000 creators, social media managers, and entrepreneurs answered, and it gives no exact count.

The results are heavy. 91.91% said content creation is mostly negative. 91.69% said the same about strategy and planning. 78.53% said that about analytics and reporting. Over 75% said they feel expected to do too many things at once.
Metricool's page also gives 75.40% for that same idea in another section, and it does not explain the difference. Treat the exact figure with care. The direction is clear either way.
Chrome cannot fix a workload that size. Profiles and tab groups cut the clutter that makes a day feel like too much. They do not reduce the number of posts a brand expects.
Where Lazur helps in Chrome on Mac
Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option and Command together, to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud.
Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. You still do the clicking.
Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Chrome or any other app. Think of it as a second pair of eyes, not a second pair of hands.

Research is the one job that runs in the background. Lazur runs it in its own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. The job comes back with a summary and a report. Your client tabs stay where they are.
Dictation and drafting for social media replies

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. In Chrome, click into the reply box, hold fn, and speak. Read the text once before you send it. A wrong handle is easy to miss when you speak fast.

Snippets help with the lines you type every day. Store a shipping answer or a refund policy as a snippet. The personal dictionary catches brand names, product names, and handles that spell check keeps changing.
Lazur also drafts text when you ask. Ask for three short replies to a DM, then edit the one you like. A draft gives you a starting point. The final words still need your judgment.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Dictation is unlimited on Pro and Power.

blocks.title: Read it once before it goes live
blocks.text: Dictate a first draft, then read it once. Client brands rarely recover from a wrong handle or a wrong date in a public reply.
Canva and Chrome in the same workday

If you make graphics in Canva, keep Canva in the same profile as the scheduler. Put it in a tab group called Visuals, next to the scheduler tab. The [Canva guide for social media managers on Mac](/for/social-media-managers/canva) covers resizing, scheduling, and common fixes.
Setup checklist for social media managers this week

items: Update Chrome, then check Chrome > About Google Chrome.
Create one profile per client and name each one after the brand.
Pin the scheduler and the main inbox in each profile.
Make a Replies group and a Reports group for each client.
Set a fixed daily check, such as 9:00, and add it to Reminders.
Get Lazur from the [download page](/download). The Pro trial lasts 3 days, needs no credit card, and starts when you first open the app.

blocks.text: Check the [pricing page](/pricing) before you choose a plan. Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually. Power is $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.
Start small. Use one profile, one group, and one daily check. Add more once that holds for a week.

faq.question: Do I need a separate Chrome profile for every client?
faq.answer: Not always, but it helps. A profile keeps bookmarks, history, passwords, and settings apart. If two clients share one tool and one login, a single profile can work. Separate profiles stop mix-ups when you move fast.

faq.question: Is a Chrome profile a security measure?
faq.answer: No. Google's help page does not describe profiles as a security boundary. Anyone with access to your Mac can switch to any profile on it. Lock your Mac when you step away.

faq.question: How do I switch Chrome profiles on a Mac?
faq.answer: Click the profile icon at the top right of the Chrome window, then choose the profile. If you cannot find the icon, ask Lazur where it is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.

faq.question: What happens if I remove a Chrome profile?
faq.answer: Removing a profile permanently erases its bookmarks, history, passwords, and settings from the computer. Export anything you need before you remove it.

faq.question: Which Chrome version is current on Mac?
faq.answer: The latest verified stable Mac release in the sources is Chrome 152, released September 1, 2026. Check Chrome > About Google Chrome to see your own version.

faq.question: Will Chrome 151 or later run on macOS 12?
faq.answer: Chrome 150 is the last release that supports macOS 12. Chrome 151 and later no longer support it. Existing installs keep running, but they stop receiving updates.

faq.question: How much time should a social media manager plan for daily checks?
faq.answer: Hootsuite's guideline estimates put replies at 30 to 60 minutes, mention checks at 15 to 30 minutes, and scheduled post reviews at 10 to 15 minutes. These are estimates, not survey data.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons in Chrome for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It points at things, answers out loud, and guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

faq.question: Is Lazur a Chrome extension?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a Mac app and is not a plugin or add-in for any app. Its background research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
